1. **Primary paper — “EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents.”** Introduces a meta-agent that jointly adapts the user simulator, environment, rewards, and RL configuration. Authors: Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).  
   URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523

2. **Official EAU project page.** Companion site linked directly from the paper, covering the same authors and affiliations above.  
   URL: https://eau-meta-agent.github.io/

3. **Pith paper review.** An independent AI-generated critique of EAU; it highlights the reported performance gains but questions whether comparisons use matched compute budgets. People involved: the six paper authors listed above.  
   URL: https://pith.science/paper/2610.16523

4. **Min Cai’s research page.** The first author describes EAU as work on continually learning agents that co-evolve with their environments. Min Cai is a PhD student at the University of Alberta, supervised by co-author Xi Ye.  
   URL: https://henrycai11.github.io/

The exact query primarily resolves to this newly submitted October 2026 paper; most other results are mirrors, summaries, or index pages for the same work.

1. **Official arXiv paper — “EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents.”** Authors: Min Cai (University of Alberta), Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore), Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology), Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher), and Xi Ye (University of Alberta; Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute/Amii). Submitted October 12, 2026.  
   URL: [https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16523)

2. **Official EAU project page.** Presents the framework, reported results, and the same author–affiliation mapping; Min Cai and Dan Zhang are marked as equal contributors.  
   URL: [https://eau-meta-agent.github.io/](https://eau-meta-agent.github.io/)

3. **Independent AI-generated paper review on Pith.** Covers the same six authors and institutions. It views the framework as promising but flags unmatched compute budgets and limited reproducibility as important caveats.  
   URL: [https://pith.science/paper/2610.16523](https://pith.science/paper/2610.16523)
